generations.outcome: Superseded by a different question, not by a losing number. G1's metrics are its own and stand unedited; what changed is the unit of analysis. This project's charter opens on a merchant-level problem — a pattern only visible at the merchant-week level, which a transaction scorer cannot see — so G2 started from a new thesis and a new harness rather than tuning G1.
generations.thesis: Every merchant carries a rupee-denominated risk budget; a reinforcement-learning policy spends it under a hard mathematical constraint, and a deterministic safety filter holds final veto. The question it answers is "how much risk can this merchant afford right now", asked per transaction.
generations.title: Constrained-RL merchant risk manager

generations.outcome: The pre-registered claim failed and was reported rather than tuned away. Underneath it sat a larger finding: on the held-out test window a uniform random score beat every fitted model on the savings metric, which is a property of the metric at this generator's 20% prevalence rather than a property of any model. Every savings number G2 published is printed net of that floor, with PR-AUC beside it.
generations.thesis: Run a Hidden Markov Model over each merchant's transaction stream, update a belief over four latent risk states with every new window, and convert that belief into pass / review / hold under per-merchant cost economics and a fixed analyst budget.
generations.title: Per-merchant HMM sentinel

generations.outcome: The test split stayed shut: the pre-registered gate that governs it failed on both conjuncts, and the threshold it was anchored to was itself invalidated by this cycle's regeneration — recorded as a pre-registration error rather than re-anchored after the fact. Every G3 number is validation-split. Four new rungs were built and scored on real cycle-4 data; all four were NOT ADOPTED and documented with numbers.
generations.thesis: Fix the generator and the evaluation harness first, seal them, then race a ladder of policies against explicit floors — five seeds, both exposure arms, every rung adopted only if it beats the previous one by a margin declared before the run.
generations.title: The rung ladder, on a fixed generator and a sealed harness

naming.note: The public labels G1/G2/G3 exist because the internal vocabulary collides: the charter calls the HMM sentinel 'v1' and this tree 'v2', while the constrained-RL tree in the sibling repository calls itself 'v1'. No charter, lock or results file was edited to introduce these labels; this map is how the two vocabularies reconcile.
